elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed ... The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Pre-existing favourable language retained unchanged.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 21.1 contains only the fees limb ("the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim"); there is no "greater of ... USD 1,000,000" floor. To reach preferred, insert "the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The consequential/indirect damages exclusion (presumably § 21.2) is not among the cited or rendered paragraphs; the rationale asserts it is mutual but no operative text is supplied for verification.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 (retained): "'Excluded Claims' means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations ...", and § 21.1 opens "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 expressly lists "data-protection, or security obligations" within Excluded Claims, which sit outside the § 21.1 cap.
§ 21.3: "its indemnification obligations" is an Excluded Claim, excepted from the cap by § 21.1.
§ 21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
§ 21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
§ 21.3: "... or fraud" within the Excluded Claims definition.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3: "or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 carves out only "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services" — "Fees" remains the narrow defined term (§ 1.5/1.6: the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) and is further qualified by "undisputed" and "conforming Services". A narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer's payment obligations as a whole.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual" — untouched by the redline.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 21.1: "shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim." The de-capitalised "fees" plus the express reference to "this Agreement and all Order Forms" defeats the illusory § 1.5 definition (Implementation Fee only, first Order Form) and yields a genuine 12-month fee basis. The deterministic check flagged false, but in substance the twelve-month fee measure is present; the check appears keyed to the capitalised/"twelve (12)" formatting rather than substance.
§ 21.3 Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations"; § 21.1 excepts Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 Excluded Claims include "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the mutual cap, the four required carve-outs (indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct) survive untouched, and the single edit converts the illusory basis (defined "Fees" = one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form) into fees paid or payable under this Agreement and all Order Forms over the preceding twelve months.

Preferred is not complete: (i) no "greater of ... USD 1,000,000" floor in § 21.1; (ii) the payment carve-out in § 21.3 is limited to "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" using the narrow defined term, so Customer's payment obligations as a whole are not excluded from capped damages; (iii) the mutuality of the indirect/consequential damages exclusion cannot be verified because § 21.2 was not cited or rendered.

Minimality holds: the operation changes only the cap basis words ("the Fees ... under the first Order Form" to "the fees ... under this Agreement and all Order Forms"); the mutuality sentence, the Excluded Claims list, the payment carve-out and §§ 1.5-1.6 are all retained verbatim, with no added survival tails, procedures or extra carve-outs.

Intent is preserved: no cross-reference is broken and no term is left undefined — lowercase "fees" is used in its ordinary sense and the retained capitalised "Fees" in § 21.3 and § 1.7 continues to operate. Residual drafting risk to monitor: a reader could argue the lowercase usage was inadvertent; if the counterparty resists, the cleaner cure is to amend § 1.5 to define "Fees" as all fees payable under this Agreement and all Order Forms rather than relying on capitalisation.

If pressing to preferred, the two operative repairs are: amend § 21.1 to read "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable ... and (b) USD 1,000,000", and amend the last sentence of § 21.3 to read "Customer's obligation to pay amounts due under this Agreement and any Order Form is not damages and is not limited by this Section."
